points.t: Pearly papule with a rolled edge and fine vessels, or a sore that bleeds, crusts and never heals, on sun-exposed skin.
UV damage switches on the Hedgehog pathway (PTCH1/SMO). Gorlin syndrome: inherited PTCH1 loss.
Routine referral (NG12 1.7.5); suspected cancer pathway if site or size makes delay matter (1.7.6).
Deep periocular and nasal BCCs; ill-defined morphoeic BCC; trigeminal trophic syndrome as a mimic.

cause.lead: Decades of UV switch on a growth pathway in basal cells.
points: **UV**: intermittent intense and cumulative; latency 20–50 years. Fair skin, age, male sex.
**Hedgehog pathway**: PTCH1 loss or SMO activation (why vismodegib and sonidegib work).
**Other risks**: previous BCC, radiotherapy, arsenic, immunosuppression, hydrochlorothiazide.
**Gorlin syndrome**: inherited PTCH1; many BCCs young, palmar pits, jaw cysts. Avoid radiotherapy.

visuals.caption: Nodular BCC: pearly surface nodule with branching vessels and central crust; nests of basaloid tumour cells in the dermis beneath.
visuals.alt: Skin cross-section through a nodular basal cell carcinoma

features.lead: About 80–85% arise on the head and neck. Slow, locally destructive.
points: **Pearly, translucent** papule or nodule with a **rolled edge**.
**Telangiectasia** over the surface; central ulcer or crust (‘rodent ulcer’).
A facial sore that **won’t heal for 4+ weeks** in an older adult: BCC until proved otherwise.

visuals.caption: Shaded: the high-risk central face ‘H-zone’ (nose, eyelids, lips, ears, temples), where margins matter most and Mohs is often chosen.
visuals.alt: Front and side views of a head with the central H-zone shaded

variants.title: Subtypes to recognise

items.name: Nodular
items.t: Commonest. Pearly nodule, rolled edge, telangiectasia, central ulcer.

items.name: Superficial
items.t: Pink, scaly thin plaque with a thread-like pearly edge.

items.name: Morphoeic
items.t: Scar-like, waxy, ill-defined; spreads unseen. High-risk.

items.name: Pigmented
items.t: Brown-blue-grey; commoner in skin of colour; melanoma DDx.

variants.more: Also: basosquamous (behaves like SCC), micronodular (high-risk histology), fibroepithelioma of Pinkus (pink pedunculated lower-back papule).

points: Slow growth; bleeds, crusts, never fully heals.
UV exposure, fair skin, previous BCC (~40% get another in 3 years).
Blue-grey ovoid nests; spoke-wheel and leaf-like areas; shiny white structures.
Skin cancer team: **punch or excision biopsy**.
Histology: basaloid nests, peripheral palisading, retraction clefts.

cards.name: Sebaceous hyperplasia
cards.clue: Yellowish umbilicated facial papules, often multiple.

cards.name: Intradermal naevus
cards.clue: Soft, symmetrical; vessels out of focus.

cards.name: Amelanotic melanoma
cards.clue: New, growing pink lesion: do not reassure.

cards.name: Bowen’s disease
cards.clue: Persistent, well-demarcated scaly red plaque (vs superficial BCC).

cards.name: Trigeminal trophic syndrome
cards.clue: Crescent ulcer of the nasal ala sparing the tip; numbness, picking. Biopsy.

differentials.more: Also: eczema or psoriasis plaque (vs superficial BCC), morphoea or scar (vs morphoeic), DFSP, molluscum, clear cell acanthoma.

manage.lead: The IP recognises and refers. Specialist teams treat (BAD 2021).

flow.sub: Do not freeze, curette or apply imiquimod to an undiagnosed lesion.

flow.q: Could delay matter because of site or size? (eye, nose, large, fast-growing)

flow.t: Refer within 1 working day of deciding

rx.note: Including nodular BCC on the face.
H-zone, morphoeic, recurrent with another high-risk factor.

points: **Radiotherapy** if unfit or unwilling (avoid in Gorlin and the young).

limits.t: H-zone; M-zone > 10 mm, L-zone > 20 mm; poorly defined; recurrent; immunosuppressed; prior RT; aggressive histology; perineural; depth > 6 mm.
5-year recurrence < 5% after surgery for low-risk primary BCC.
Only low-risk BCCs by accredited clinicians (NICE IOG).

items.t: Near the **eye, nose or ear**, large, fast-growing or recurrent: consider the **suspected cancer pathway** (NG12 1.7.6).
Typical BCC at a low-risk site: routine dermatology referral (NG12 1.7.5).
Multiple BCCs young, palmar pits or jaw cysts: think **Gorlin syndrome**.
Never treat an **undiagnosed** pigmented or nodular lesion: refer for diagnosis first.

pearls.t: **Medicines review**: hydrochlorothiazide (NMSC risk), long-term voriconazole, azathioprine.
**Imiquimod**: bedtime, wash off after ~8 h; redness and crusting mean it is working.
SPF 30+ high-UVA, shade, hats (NICE NG34). Monthly self-check.
Hedgehog inhibitors: pregnancy prevention; cramps, taste and weight loss.
Care homes: report facial lesions not healing after 4 weeks.
Continue aspirin for biopsy or skin surgery (BSDS 2023).

quiz.q: What is the NICE NG12 referral speed for a typical BCC?
quiz.a: Routine referral (1.7.5); consider the suspected cancer pathway only if site or size makes delay matter (1.7.6).
Arborising (tree-like) vessels in sharp focus; also blue-grey ovoid nests.

quiz.q: First-line treatment for most BCCs, including nodular BCC on the face?
quiz.a: Standard surgical excision (4 mm margin low-risk, ≥ 5 mm high-risk); Mohs for high-risk or recurrent.

quiz.q: Which mimic causes a crescent ulcer of the nasal ala that spares the tip?
quiz.a: Trigeminal trophic syndrome. Biopsy to exclude BCC.

quiz.q: What must an IP never do with a suspected BCC?
quiz.a: Freeze, curette or apply imiquimod to an undiagnosed lesion. Refer for diagnosis first.
